title: Erdős 1049 Padé exterior determinants: channel divisibility and sign-controlled noncancellation

concepts.label: Padé exterior determinant
concepts.note: The integer determinant Un*Vm-Um*Vn of two coefficient rows.

concepts.label: coefficient-channel common divisor
concepts.note: A divisor shared by both U coefficients or by both V coefficients.

concepts.label: positive Padé errors
concepts.note: Strict positivity of both real linear-form errors in the two selected rows.

concepts.label: alternating first-coefficient signs
concepts.note: One U coefficient is strictly negative and the other strictly positive.

concepts.label: sign-controlled determinant noncancellation
concepts.note: The determinant sign, and hence nonvanishing, forced by positive errors and alternating U signs.

concepts.label: finite arithmetic authority boundary
concepts.note: The zone proves abstract divisibility and sign lemmas only; it supplies no Padé family, analytic remainder positivity or decay, coefficient-sign theorem, primitive local gain, or irrationality result.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED DIVISIBILITY INTERFACE: if d divides both Un and Um, then d divides rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm; symmetrically, if d divides both Vn and Vm, then d divides the same exterior determinant.
statement_nodes.engine: Factor the common divisor from the two terms of Un*Vm-Um*Vn in the selected coefficient channel.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary determinant divisibility over the integers; no novelty or priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorems do not produce a nonunit divisor, a growing prime-power valuation, primitive Padé rows, or a favorable local-to-Archimedean balance. Separate divisors from the U and V channels each divide the determinant, but their product is not asserted to divide it without an additional coprimality argument.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL SIGN PACKET: if both rational Padé errors are strictly positive and Un<0<Um, then the exterior determinant is strictly positive; if both errors are strictly positive and Um<0<Un, then it is strictly negative. In either alternating-sign configuration the determinant is nonzero.
open_antecedents: For application to an actual adjacent Padé family, strict positivity of both real errors rationalPadeError S Un Vn and rationalPadeError S Um Vm.
For the same selected adjacent rows, one of the two strict alternating sign patterns Un<0<Um or Um<0<Un.
statement_nodes.engine: Use the exact real determinant identity Um*error_n-Un*error_m; positive errors and the two alternating coefficient signs make both contributions have the same strict sign, then cast the result back to the integer determinant.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary sign analysis of the exterior-determinant identity; no analytic positivity theorem or novelty claim is supplied.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The abstract implications are proved, but the intended Padé application still needs an actual coefficient family with positive remainders and alternating U signs. The packet gives no determinant-size bound, no local divisibility gain, no remainder decay, and no irrationality or transcendence conclusion.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The channel lemmas provide arithmetic divisibility of the determinant, while the sign packet provides conditional Archimedean noncancellation; neither supplies the other's hypotheses or a favorable size-versus-divisor inequality.
